Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".

- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

content.content:
1	---
2	name: paper-refinement
3	description: Step 5 论文迭代修改循环——Reviewer 评分循环 + 收敛判断 + paper_checklist 注入，max 5 轮。Paper Agent 进入 Step 5 时 Read 本 skill。
4	scope: global
5	tags:
6	  - workflow
7	  - research
8	  - writing
9	  - academic
10	  - review
11	version: 1
12	roles:
13	  - paper_agent
14	---
15	
16	# Step 5 — Iterative Refinement
17	
18	Step 4 全部章节落盘后，Paper Agent 进入 Step 5：把全文递交 Reviewer 评分，按反馈修改，直到收敛。
19	
20	**核心约束**：
21	- 串行——一轮 Reviewer 返回结果处理完才进下一轮，禁止并发请求
22	- 评分驱动——overall 提升才 accept 本轮，下降则 git revert
23	- 上限 5 轮——硬约束，达到上限即停，不论分数
24	
25	## 状态记录（git 是 truth source）
26	
27	每轮修改前 commit 当前论文目录，作为 revert 锚点。无需额外 state 文件。
28	
29	```
30	git -C projects/{project} add paper/
31	git -C projects/{project} commit -m "[paper] refinement round {N-1}"
32	```
33	
34	Round N 的 commit message 用 `N-1`，即 round 1 修改前 commit `round 0`（Step 4 落盘后的初稿）。
35	
36	## 单轮流程
37	
38	```
39	Round N（N = 1..5）：
40	
41	1. git commit 当前版本（message: "[paper] refinement round N-1"）
42	   └── 落地评分下降时的 revert 锚点
43	
44	2. 组装审查请求：
45	   - read_project_file("paper_checklist.yaml") — 用户自定义必查项
46	   - 拼 LaTeX 全文（或 Patch 模式下的差异）+ writing_plan.yaml 路径
47	   - 末尾追加 "## 用户自定义必查项"（见下方"checklist 注入格式"）
48	
49	3. paper_agent_request_review(text=组装后的请求, project=...)
50	   └── 请求末尾追加维度提醒："除标准的 Originality/Clarity/Soundness/Significance/Presentation 维度外，请额外检查：叙事一致性（各章节是否讲同一个故事）、贡献-范围对齐（Intro contribution ↔ 正文 section 1:1）、去 AI 风格（em-dash、-ing、filler words）。参考 reviewer-audit-checklist §7。"
51	   └── Reviewer 通过 reviewer_post_to_director 回传评分
52	
53	4. 解析 Reviewer 响应：
54	   - 维度分（Originality/Clarity/Soundness/Significance/Presentation，1-4）
55	   - overall（1-10）
56	   - 各条具体问题 severity（critical/warning/info）
57	   - checklist 项 PASS/FAIL
58	   ★ 任一 checklist FAIL → 该条问题 severity 自动按 critical 对待
59	
60	5. 按问题类型分流处理：
61	   - 事实性错误（数字不一致 / 引用错位）→ 自己用 edit_paper_section 改
62	   - 段落级叙事问题（逻辑断裂 / 强度词超限）→ spawn Worker 重写段落，回来再 edit_paper_section
63	   - 结构问题（章节顺序 / 段落归并）→ 自己用 edit_paper_section
64	   - critical 且 claim 本身无支撑 → 汇报 Director（不要自行降 claim）
65	
66	6. 全部问题处理完后判断本轮 overall 走势：
67	   - overall(N) ≥ overall(N-1) → 保留本轮修改，进入收敛判断
68	   - overall(N) <  overall(N-1) → git checkout 上一轮 commit，回退本轮所有修改，标记"本轮无进展"
69	
70	7. 收敛判断（任一满足即停）：
71	   - 全部问题为 info（无 critical / warning）
72	   - N == 5（硬上限）
73	   - 连续两轮 overall 持平（差 ≤0.1）
74	   - 连续两轮无新增 critical（critical 列表内容相同或更短）
75	
76	   未收敛且 N<5 → 进入 Round N+1
77	   已收敛 → 进入收尾（见下文）
78	```
79	
80	## checklist 注入格式
81	
82	`read_project_file("paper_checklist.yaml")` 拿到 items 后，在审查请求末尾追加：
83	
84	```
85	## 用户自定义必查项
86	以下是用户指定的必须检查的项，每项必须明确标注 PASS 或 FAIL：
87	- [chk_001] {text}
88	- [chk_002] {text}
89	...
90	
91	如果任何一项标注为 FAIL，整体 severity 自动提升为 critical（必须打回修改）。
92	```
93	
94	- checklist 为空 / 文件不存在 → 不追加该段，正常请求
95	- 不要重写 checklist 文本——保持用户原话，让 Reviewer 自己定位
96	- Dream 模式禁止注入（Dream 论文不投，格式检查无意义）
97	
98	## 修改 Worker 任务模板
99	
100	段落级修改派 Worker（不是整章重写）时：
101	
102	```
103	spawn_worker(
104	  task_type="paper_writing",
105	  project=...,
106	  task_prompt="""
107	Reviewer 在 {section} 章发现以下问题，需要你修改对应段落：
108	
109	【问题位置】{paragraph_id / 行号}
110	【问题描述】{Reviewer 原文}
111	【建议方向】{Reviewer 给的方向}
112	
113	当前段落原文：
114	```latex
115	{原文片段}
116	```
117	
118	参考资料：
119	- 写作规范：Read skills/global/latex-paper.skill.md + red-section.skill.md
120	- registry 切片：{相关 exp_id 列表}
121	- 同章节已有内容：{section}.tex 整章
122	- 引用：references.bib（只用已 verified 条目，未验证标 [UNVERIFIED]）
123	
124	要求：
125	- 只改问题段落，不动其他内容
126	- 输出修改后的段落 latex（标记 old / new）
127	- 不要画图、不要补实验
128	- 改完即返回，不写额外说明
129	"""
130	)
131	```
132	
133	Worker 返回后 Paper Agent 用 `edit_paper_section(project, section, old_text=..., new_text=..., claims=..., table_cells=..., figures=...)` 落盘——`edit_paper_section` 自动同步 provenance，不会 deprecate 未触及的 claim。
134	
135	## 收敛后收尾（Step 5e）
136	
137	Reviewer 评分循环收敛后**必须执行完整三件套**——视觉 + 引用 + 溯源**全部跑完**再汇报 Director；不允许只跑一两项就提交。任一发现 critical/blocker 都要在汇报中显式列出，不得"建议提交审稿"压过失败信号。
138	
139	### 三件套执行顺序
140	
141	按下面顺序串行（每一步完成才进下一步，前一步失败不绕过）：
142	
143	```
144	1. paper-visual-review 排版检查
145	   └── Read skills/global/paper-visual-review.skill.md
146	   └── pdf_to_images(pdf_path=projects/{project}/paper/main.pdf, pages="1-N", dpi=200)
147	       逐页检查图表分辨率 / 字号 / 边距溢出 / 公式 / 引用编号 / 缺失引用占位 [?]
148	   └── cleanup_pdf_images(output_dir=<上一步返回的 output_dir>)  # 不留临时文件
149	   └── 收集 findings：[{page, severity, issue}]
150	   └── 出现 critical（图表溢出 / 缺失编号 / 公式乱码）→ 记入 visual_report，**不**立即返工，
151	       与 verify_references / check_provenance_completeness 的结果**一并汇报 Director**
152	
153	2. verify_references 最终引用验证
154	   └── verify_references(paper_dir="projects/{project}/paper", project=..., skip_online=False)
155	   └── 返回字段：status (ok/orphan_bib/missing_bib/not_found/mismatch) 按条聚合
156	   └── critical 阈值：
157	        - missing_bib（正文 \cite 但 .bib 缺）→ 必须修，否则 LaTeX 编译失败
158	        - not_found（OpenAlex 找不到）→ 疑似幻觉引用，自己 WebSearch 二次验证；仍找不到 → critical
159	        - mismatch（年份/作者偏差）→ warning
160	   └── 自己能改的小问题（missing_bib、年份） → edit_paper_section 修；改完**再调一次 verify_references** 确认通过
161	
162	3. check_provenance_completeness 溯源覆盖
163	   └── check_provenance_completeness(project=...)
164	   └── 返回：tier_distribution / untracked_numbers / invalidated_claims
165	   └── 关键阈值：
166	        - Tier 3 占比 > 30% → 必须汇报 Director（红线，不得静默交付）
167	        - Tier X（invalidated，实验失败/被作废）≥ 1 条 → critical：claim 失去支撑，汇报 Director 决策是否改 claim
168	        - untracked_numbers（正文出现但 provenance 没追踪的数字）≥ 5 → warning：派 Worker 补 provenance
169	```
170	
171	### 汇报 Director 模板
172	
173	三件套全部跑完后**统一**汇报（不要分三次发），把所有 critical/warning 列在一处便于 Director 决策：
174	
175	```
176	paper_agent_post_to_director(
177	  text="[写作进展] Step 5 收尾完成
178	         迭代轮数：{N}/5
179	         最终 overall：{score}
180	         checklist：全部 PASS / 还有 X 条 FAIL（已修复 / 待 Director 决策）
181	
182	         ===== 视觉检查 =====
183	         检查页数：{n}/{total}
184	         结论：PASS / 发现 X 条 critical + Y 条 warning
185	         {若有 critical：逐条列出 page + 描述}
186	
187	         ===== 引用验证 =====
188	         总数 X 条，已验证 Y 条
189	         critical：missing_bib X 条 + 疑似幻觉 Y 条（已尝试 WebSearch 二次验证 → 结果）
190	         warning：mismatch X 条
191	         {若有 critical：列出条目 + 已采取的修复}
192	
193	         ===== Provenance 覆盖 =====
194	         Tier 分布：T1 {a}% / T2 {b}% / T3 {c}% / TX {d}%
195	         {若 T3 > 30% 或 TX ≥ 1：列出受影响的 claim/figure/table}
196	         未追踪数字：X 个（详见 untracked_numbers）
197	
198	         ===== 建议 =====
199	         {以下任选其一}
200	         A. 视觉/引用/provenance 全部 PASS → 建议提交审稿（submit_paper_to_review）
201	         B. 存在 critical → 请 Director 决策：{具体问题列表 + 建议修复方向}
202	         C. provenance 红线触发 → 请 Director 决定：补实验 / 改 claim / 接受现状",
203	  project=...
204	)
205	```
206	
207	Director 决定是否调 `submit_paper_to_review`——Paper Agent **不**主动调，这是 Director 的权限。
208	
209	### 红线（Step 5e 不可绕过）
210	
211	1. **三件套必须全跑**：跳过任一项直接汇报 = 违规，被 Director 打回时不接受"我以为不必要"
212	2. **critical 不静默**：视觉 critical / verify_references critical / Tier X ≥ 1 / Tier 3 > 30% 必须显式写进汇报
213	3. **不主动提交审稿**：哪怕全 PASS 也只能"建议提交"，submit_paper_to_review 是 Director 权限
214	4. **修复后必须复验**：自己修了 missing_bib → 重跑 verify_references；补 provenance → 重跑 check_provenance_completeness
215	5. **Patch 模式走 Phase E**：Patch 的收尾在 Phase E（max 3 轮 Reviewer），不复用 Step 5e 全套；Phase E 自己做 check_provenance_completeness + verify_references，视觉检查可选
216	
217	## 硬约束（与 Paper Agent 红线一致）
218	
219	1. **修改前必 git commit**——没有 commit 不开新一轮，避免 revert 失败
220	2. **未验证引用不进 .bib**——Reviewer 指出新引用需求时，先 verify_references 再写入
221	3. **checklist FAIL 项必须修复**——不参与"连续两轮无新增 critical"的轮数计数，但下一轮必须解决
222	4. **overall 下降必 revert**——不允许"将就一下"
223	5. **不自行降 claim**——claim 无支撑是 Director 决策，Paper Agent 只能改表述强度，不能改 claim 内容
224	6. **Patch / Dream 模式不走本 skill**——Patch 走 Phase E（max 3 轮），Dream 跳过 Reviewer 迭代
225	
226	## 与 Reviewer 评分模板的合约
227	
228	Reviewer 在 `prompts/roles/reviewer.md` §5.3 已规定返回格式：
229	
230	```
231	[写作评审] 轮次 N/5
232	维度评分（1-4）：Originality / Clarity / Soundness / Significance / Presentation
233	Overall（1-10）：
234	## 用户自定义必查项（如审查请求含 paper_checklist）
235	- [chk_id]: PASS / FAIL — 理由
236	## 具体问题
237	- [severity] 位置 + 描述 + 建议
238	```
239	
240	Paper Agent 解析时按位置抓字段——Reviewer 偶尔会漏维度分，**漏了的当作 4（满分）处理**，避免误判 overall 下降。
241

file.content:
---
name: paper-refinement
description: Step 5 论文迭代修改循环——Reviewer 评分循环 + 收敛判断 + paper_checklist 注入，max 5 轮。Paper Agent 进入 Step 5 时 Read 本 skill。
scope: global
tags:
  - workflow
  - research
  - writing
  - academic
  - review
version: 1
roles:
  - paper_agent
---

# Step 5 — Iterative Refinement

Step 4 全部章节落盘后，Paper Agent 进入 Step 5：把全文递交 Reviewer 评分，按反馈修改，直到收敛。

**核心约束**：
- 串行——一轮 Reviewer 返回结果处理完才进下一轮，禁止并发请求
- 评分驱动——overall 提升才 accept 本轮，下降则 git revert
- 上限 5 轮——硬约束，达到上限即停，不论分数

## 状态记录（git 是 truth source）

每轮修改前 commit 当前论文目录，作为 revert 锚点。无需额外 state 文件。

```
git -C projects/{project} add paper/
git -C projects/{project} commit -m "[paper] refinement round {N-1}"
```

Round N 的 commit message 用 `N-1`，即 round 1 修改前 commit `round 0`（Step 4 落盘后的初稿）。

## 单轮流程

```
Round N（N = 1..5）：

1. git commit 当前版本（message: "[paper] refinement round N-1"）
   └── 落地评分下降时的 revert 锚点

2. 组装审查请求：
   - read_project_file("paper_checklist.yaml") — 用户自定义必查项
   - 拼 LaTeX 全文（或 Patch 模式下的差异）+ writing_plan.yaml 路径
   - 末尾追加 "## 用户自定义必查项"（见下方"checklist 注入格式"）

3. paper_agent_request_review(text=组装后的请求, project=...)
   └── 请求末尾追加维度提醒："除标准的 Originality/Clarity/Soundness/Significance/Presentation 维度外，请额外检查：叙事一致性（各章节是否讲同一个故事）、贡献-范围对齐（Intro contribution ↔ 正文 section 1:1）、去 AI 风格（em-dash、-ing、filler words）。参考 reviewer-audit-checklist §7。"
   └── Reviewer 通过 reviewer_post_to_director 回传评分

4. 解析 Reviewer 响应：
   - 维度分（Originality/Clarity/Soundness/Significance/Presentation，1-4）
   - overall（1-10）
   - 各条具体问题 severity（critical/warning/info）
   - checklist 项 PASS/FAIL
   ★ 任一 checklist FAIL → 该条问题 severity 自动按 critical 对待

5. 按问题类型分流处理：
   - 事实性错误（数字不一致 / 引用错位）→ 自己用 edit_paper_section 改
   - 段落级叙事问题（逻辑断裂 / 强度词超限）→ spawn Worker 重写段落，回来再 edit_paper_section
   - 结构问题（章节顺序 / 段落归并）→ 自己用 edit_paper_section
   - critical 且 claim 本身无支撑 → 汇报 Director（不要自行降 claim）

6. 全部问题处理完后判断本轮 overall 走势：
   - overall(N) ≥ overall(N-1) → 保留本轮修改，进入收敛判断
   - overall(N) <  overall(N-1) → git checkout 上一轮 commit，回退本轮所有修改，标记"本轮无进展"

7. 收敛判断（任一满足即停）：
   - 全部问题为 info（无 critical / warning）
   - N == 5（硬上限）
   - 连续两轮 overall 持平（差 ≤0.1）
   - 连续两轮无新增 critical（critical 列表内容相同或更短）

   未收敛且 N<5 → 进入 Round N+1
   已收敛 → 进入收尾（见下文）
```

## checklist 注入格式

`read_project_file("paper_checklist.yaml")` 拿到 items 后，在审查请求末尾追加：

```
## 用户自定义必查项
以下是用户指定的必须检查的项，每项必须明确标注 PASS 或 FAIL：
- [chk_001] {text}
- [chk_002] {text}
...

如果任何一项标注为 FAIL，整体 severity 自动提升为 critical（必须打回修改）。
```

- checklist 为空 / 文件不存在 → 不追加该段，正常请求
- 不要重写 checklist 文本——保持用户原话，让 Reviewer 自己定位
- Dream 模式禁止注入（Dream 论文不投，格式检查无意义）

## 修改 Worker 任务模板

段落级修改派 Worker（不是整章重写）时：

```
spawn_worker(
  task_type="paper_writing",
  project=...,
  task_prompt="""
Reviewer 在 {section} 章发现以下问题，需要你修改对应段落：

【问题位置】{paragraph_id / 行号}
【问题描述】{Reviewer 原文}
【建议方向】{Reviewer 给的方向}

当前段落原文：
```latex
{原文片段}
```

参考资料：
- 写作规范：Read skills/global/latex-paper.skill.md + red-section.skill.md
- registry 切片：{相关 exp_id 列表}
- 同章节已有内容：{section}.tex 整章
- 引用：references.bib（只用已 verified 条目，未验证标 [UNVERIFIED]）

要求：
- 只改问题段落，不动其他内容
- 输出修改后的段落 latex（标记 old / new）
- 不要画图、不要补实验
- 改完即返回，不写额外说明
"""
)
```

Worker 返回后 Paper Agent 用 `edit_paper_section(project, section, old_text=..., new_text=..., claims=..., table_cells=..., figures=...)` 落盘——`edit_paper_section` 自动同步 provenance，不会 deprecate 未触及的 claim。

## 收敛后收尾（Step 5e）

Reviewer 评分循环收敛后**必须执行完整三件套**——视觉 + 引用 + 溯源**全部跑完**再汇报 Director；不允许只跑一两项就提交。任一发现 critical/blocker 都要在汇报中显式列出，不得"建议提交审稿"压过失败信号。

### 三件套执行顺序

按下面顺序串行（每一步完成才进下一步，前一步失败不绕过）：

```
1. paper-visual-review 排版检查
   └── Read skills/global/paper-visual-review.skill.md
   └── pdf_to_images(pdf_path=projects/{project}/paper/main.pdf, pages="1-N", dpi=200)
       逐页检查图表分辨率 / 字号 / 边距溢出 / 公式 / 引用编号 / 缺失引用占位 [?]
   └── cleanup_pdf_images(output_dir=<上一步返回的 output_dir>)  # 不留临时文件
   └── 收集 findings：[{page, severity, issue}]
   └── 出现 critical（图表溢出 / 缺失编号 / 公式乱码）→ 记入 visual_report，**不**立即返工，
       与 verify_references / check_provenance_completeness 的结果**一并汇报 Director**

2. verify_references 最终引用验证
   └── verify_references(paper_dir="projects/{project}/paper", project=..., skip_online=False)
   └── 返回字段：status (ok/orphan_bib/missing_bib/not_found/mismatch) 按条聚合
   └── critical 阈值：
        - missing_bib（正文 \cite 但 .bib 缺）→ 必须修，否则 LaTeX 编译失败
        - not_found（OpenAlex 找不到）→ 疑似幻觉引用，自己 WebSearch 二次验证；仍找不到 → critical
        - mismatch（年份/作者偏差）→ warning
   └── 自己能改的小问题（missing_bib、年份） → edit_paper_section 修；改完**再调一次 verify_references** 确认通过

3. check_provenance_completeness 溯源覆盖
   └── check_provenance_completeness(project=...)
   └── 返回：tier_distribution / untracked_numbers / invalidated_claims
   └── 关键阈值：
        - Tier 3 占比 > 30% → 必须汇报 Director（红线，不得静默交付）
        - Tier X（invalidated，实验失败/被作废）≥ 1 条 → critical：claim 失去支撑，汇报 Director 决策是否改 claim
        - untracked_numbers（正文出现但 provenance 没追踪的数字）≥ 5 → warning：派 Worker 补 provenance
```

### 汇报 Director 模板

三件套全部跑完后**统一**汇报（不要分三次发），把所有 critical/warning 列在一处便于 Director 决策：

```
paper_agent_post_to_director(
  text="[写作进展] Step 5 收尾完成
         迭代轮数：{N}/5
         最终 overall：{score}
         checklist：全部 PASS / 还有 X 条 FAIL（已修复 / 待 Director 决策）

         ===== 视觉检查 =====
         检查页数：{n}/{total}
         结论：PASS / 发现 X 条 critical + Y 条 warning
         {若有 critical：逐条列出 page + 描述}

         ===== 引用验证 =====
         总数 X 条，已验证 Y 条
         critical：missing_bib X 条 + 疑似幻觉 Y 条（已尝试 WebSearch 二次验证 → 结果）
         warning：mismatch X 条
         {若有 critical：列出条目 + 已采取的修复}

         ===== Provenance 覆盖 =====
         Tier 分布：T1 {a}% / T2 {b}% / T3 {c}% / TX {d}%
         {若 T3 > 30% 或 TX ≥ 1：列出受影响的 claim/figure/table}
         未追踪数字：X 个（详见 untracked_numbers）

         ===== 建议 =====
         {以下任选其一}
         A. 视觉/引用/provenance 全部 PASS → 建议提交审稿（submit_paper_to_review）
         B. 存在 critical → 请 Director 决策：{具体问题列表 + 建议修复方向}
         C. provenance 红线触发 → 请 Director 决定：补实验 / 改 claim / 接受现状",
  project=...
)
```

Director 决定是否调 `submit_paper_to_review`——Paper Agent **不**主动调，这是 Director 的权限。

### 红线（Step 5e 不可绕过）

1. **三件套必须全跑**：跳过任一项直接汇报 = 违规，被 Director 打回时不接受"我以为不必要"
2. **critical 不静默**：视觉 critical / verify_references critical / Tier X ≥ 1 / Tier 3 > 30% 必须显式写进汇报
3. **不主动提交审稿**：哪怕全 PASS 也只能"建议提交"，submit_paper_to_review 是 Director 权限
4. **修复后必须复验**：自己修了 missing_bib → 重跑 verify_references；补 provenance → 重跑 check_provenance_completeness
5. **Patch 模式走 Phase E**：Patch 的收尾在 Phase E（max 3 轮 Reviewer），不复用 Step 5e 全套；Phase E 自己做 check_provenance_completeness + verify_references，视觉检查可选

## 硬约束（与 Paper Agent 红线一致）

1. **修改前必 git commit**——没有 commit 不开新一轮，避免 revert 失败
2. **未验证引用不进 .bib**——Reviewer 指出新引用需求时，先 verify_references 再写入
3. **checklist FAIL 项必须修复**——不参与"连续两轮无新增 critical"的轮数计数，但下一轮必须解决
4. **overall 下降必 revert**——不允许"将就一下"
5. **不自行降 claim**——claim 无支撑是 Director 决策，Paper Agent 只能改表述强度，不能改 claim 内容
6. **Patch / Dream 模式不走本 skill**——Patch 走 Phase E（max 3 轮），Dream 跳过 Reviewer 迭代

## 与 Reviewer 评分模板的合约

Reviewer 在 `prompts/roles/reviewer.md` §5.3 已规定返回格式：

```
[写作评审] 轮次 N/5
维度评分（1-4）：Originality / Clarity / Soundness / Significance / Presentation
Overall（1-10）：
## 用户自定义必查项（如审查请求含 paper_checklist）
- [chk_id]: PASS / FAIL — 理由
## 具体问题
- [severity] 位置 + 描述 + 建议
```

Paper Agent 解析时按位置抓字段——Reviewer 偶尔会漏维度分，**漏了的当作 4（满分）处理**，避免误判 overall 下降。

content.content:
1	---
2	name: paper-quality-lessons
3	description: NeurIPS 投稿实战经验总结——人工审查中提炼的写作规范、审查清单、常见反模式。Paper Agent / Reviewer / Director 写论文或审查论文时加载。
4	allowed-tools: [Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep]
5	scope: global
6	version: 1
7	tags:
8	  - writing
9	  - paper
10	  - quality
11	  - checklist
12	  - review
13	roles:
14	  - agent
15	  - reviewer
16	  - director
17	  - paper_agent
18	---
19	
20	# 论文写作质量指南（NeurIPS 实战经验）
21	
22	> 来源：2026 年 NeurIPS 投稿期间，从 20+ 项目的人工审查反馈中提炼。
23	> 每条规则都源自真实的 bug / 退回 / 审稿质疑。
24	
25	---
26	
27	## 一、数据诚信与溯源（最高优先级）
28	
29	### 1.1 数字必须有源头
30	
31	- 论文中**每一个数字**必须可追溯到 registry 实验 ID 或原始结果文件
32	- 禁止凭记忆写数字——必须 `cat result.json | head` + `ls -la` 附上文件证据
33	- 计算值（均值、标准差、DID、delta）必须独立重算，不信 Agent 第一手汇报
34	- `paper_provenance.yaml` 覆盖率必须 100%，改数字必须同步更新 provenance
35	
36	> **教训（D149 事件）**：Agent 曾伪造完整的 metrics 数据包括 p-value，事后被 Reviewer 独立 parse JSON 抓出。从此所有关键数据必须 Reviewer 独立验证到字段级别。
37	
38	### 1.2 不同来源数据不能混用
39	
40	- 配对数据必须同 seed、同 c 值、同 N、同 evaluation protocol
41	- 两张表如果 protocol 不同（如 0-shot vs 8-shot），论文必须明确说明
42	- 跨 config 比较 delta 会引入系统误差——必须补跑同 config baseline 后才能比较
43	- 非等量对比必须显式标注（如 "at unmatched volumes"）
44	
45	> **教训（D027 事件）**：不同 config 文件的 baseline 不同，跨 config 比较 delta 值引入了 artifact。
46	
47	### 1.3 结论撤回后不可复活
48	
49	- 被 Director shelved 的数据（如因截断混淆），禁止重新引入论文
50	- `paper_provenance.yaml` 中 `verified: false` 的 claim，不得恢复
51	- 术语修正后不可回退（如 "same norm" → "same per-layer standard deviation"）
52	
53	---
54	
55	## 二、Claim 强度与数据匹配
56	
57	### 2.1 Claim 强度规则
58	
59	| 数据支撑 | 允许的最强表述 |
60	|----------|--------------|
61	| 单 seed, 单数据集 | "preliminary observation", "initial evidence" |
62	| 单 seed, 多数据集 | "suggestive pattern", "indicative trend" |
63	| 多 seed, 单数据集 | 报告均值±标准差，可写 "we find" |
64	| 多 seed, 多数据集 | 可用 "robust", "consistent" |
65	| 统计检验显著 | 可用 "significant", 附 p-value |
66	| 单 seed + 外推到其他条件 | 必须加限定，不能声称 "scale-invariant" 等 |
67	
68	### 2.2 禁止的过强表述
69	
70	- "remarkably stable" → 改为 "relatively stable" 或给出量化波动范围
71	- "confirmed" → 仅 "suggestive" 级别数据不能用
72	- "scale-invariant" → single-seed 验证不够
73	- "We attribute X to Y" → 如果是假说，必须改为 "We hypothesize" + "requiring causal verification"
74	- "roughly twice" → 实际比值必须在 1.8x-2.2x 才能用，否则改为更准确的近似
75	- "domain-agnostic" → 改为 "robust across N domains tested"
76	
77	### 2.3 Claim 降级机制
78	
79	当证据不足以支撑独立 claim 时，应降级为 discussion 中的定性讨论，而非删除。具体做法：
80	- 独立 contribution → Discussion 段落
81	- 硬 claim → 加 caveat 的软 claim
82	- 正文数字 → 移入 Appendix
83	
84	---
85	
86	## 三、叙事与 Storytelling
87	
88	### 3.1 结构原则
89	
90	- 核心 paradox/发现之间必须有**过渡句**桥接，不能让读者在关键处断线
91	- Introduction 每条 Contribution 必须有对应的 section/table 支撑
92	- Discussion 不应重复 Results 的具体数字——引用表格编号
93	- 同一解释不要在多处重复推导——主文写一次 + 指向 Appendix
94	- Limitations 段不要写成一个 17 行大段——拆分为 2-3 个子段按主题分组
95	
96	### 3.2 冷引用（Cold Reference）
97	
98	- 任何首次出现的概念必须有上文铺垫
99	- Introduction 贡献列表中不能突然出现未被提及的模型/方法名
100	
101	### 3.3 不要用旧叙事套新数字
102	
103	新 baseline 出来后若 delta 大幅变化，Section 的叙事逻辑必须重写，不是简单替换数字。
104	
105	### 3.4 Contingency Plan
106	
107	关键实验结果不确定时需预写两套叙事（如 "若结果 A → 叙事 A"、"若结果 B → 叙事 B"），实验完成后选择正确版本。提交前必须确认只留了一套。
108	
109	### 3.5 不要基于中间值做叙事决策
110	
111	70% 进度时的估计往往不够稳定（尤其 GSM8K 等难度分布不均匀的 benchmark），必须等完整数据再定稿叙事。
112	
113	---
114	
115	## 四、术语与一致性
116	
117	### 4.1 术语一致性
118	
119	- 全文必须统一使用正式定义的术语，不得出现同义词漂移
120	- 术语定义后，每次使用必须完全一致（不要有时 "perturbation sensitivity" 有时 "perturbation impact"）
121	
122	### 4.2 统计量一致性
123	
124	- 两个不同的 kappa/p-value 每次出现时必须标注是哪个
125	- 同一个 metric 在不同位置的数字必须完全一致
126	- 修改任何数字后必须全文 grep 确认所有引用处同步
127	
128	### 4.3 p-value 格式
129	
130	- 无前导零、3 位小数：`p = .003`（不是 `p = 0.003`）
131	- 当非劣效性 p<0.001 实际由正向效应驱动时，必须加括注说明
132	
133	### 4.4 例子与定义必须一致
134	
135	Taxonomy 中的定义和对应示例不能自相矛盾。如果定义说 "no new content"，示例中就不能包含新信息。
136	
137	---
138	
139	## 五、投稿前检查清单（Pre-Submission Checklist）
140	
141	### 5.1 占位符扫描（硬门禁）
142	
143	提交前必须 grep 扫描，以下模式要求**零匹配**：
144	```
145	XX.XX, PLACEHOLDER, [If , TODO, TBD, \placeholder{
146	```
147	所有条件占位段落（`[If ...]`）必须替换为最终文本。
148	
149	### 5.2 编译检查
150	
151	- [ ] 编译零 error
152	- [ ] 无 `??` 未解析引用
153	- [ ] 无 > 1pt 的 overfull hbox
154	- [ ] 正文 ≤ 9 页（NeurIPS desk reject 风险）
155	- [ ] 使用当年 style file（`neurips_2026.sty`）
156	- [ ] Review 版启用行号
157	- [ ] 匿名审稿版无作者姓名、无致谢
158	
159	### 5.3 数据完整性
160	
161	- [ ] 论文所有数字与 registry/provenance 交叉验证通过
162	- [ ] 计算值（均值、标准差、DID、delta）独立重算确认
163	- [ ] 所有 evaluation protocol 差异已在论文中说明
164	- [ ] 多 seed 结果报告均值和标准差
165	- [ ] 单 seed 数据在 Limitations 中声明
166	
167	### 5.4 图表检查
168	
169	- [ ] 所有 figure PDF 存在且路径匹配
170	- [ ] 图表不超栏宽（单栏 5.5in / 全宽 6.5in）
171	- [ ] 图中字体 ≥ 7pt
172	- [ ] 小数精度全表统一
173	- [ ] 最优结果加粗、次优下划线
174	- [ ] 表格标题（caption）自包含
175	- [ ] Forest plot 等可视化无 dummy 值（CI_LO=-99 等）
176	
177	### 5.5 引用检查
178	
179	- [ ] 引用覆盖：**直接相关方法、baseline 论文、评测 benchmark 论文、理论基础**（任一缺失说明调研不充分）
180	- [ ] 引用密度与目标会议近年录用论文同量级
181	- [ ] 引用键与 bib 条目 1:1 匹配
182	- [ ] 无孤儿 bib 条目
183	- [ ] 无幻觉引用（所有被引论文实际存在）
184	- [ ] 近年论文的年份/会议准确
185	- [ ] 审稿人要求的引用全部补齐
186	
187	### 5.6 匿名化检查
188	
189	- [ ] 源代码无硬编码绝对路径（`/Users/...`, `/root/...`）
190	- [ ] 配置文件无服务器路径
191	- [ ] Git history 已清理 author 信息（用 fresh repo）
192	- [ ] 项目管理文件不得提交（AGENTS.md, memory.md, registry.yaml, task_context/ 等）
193	- [ ] API Keys 通过环境变量，无泄露
194	
195	### 5.7 会议 Checklist 填写（如目标会议要求）
196	
197	- [ ] Claims: 摘要/Introduction 准确反映实验范围
198	- [ ] Limitations: 正文 Limitations 段 + Appendix 补充
199	- [ ] Experiments: 实验设置完整（exp_id, seed, 超参, 评估 protocol）
200	- [ ] Reproducibility: 数据集公开、代码可用
201	- [ ] Statistical Significance: 多 seed 均值+标准差、置信区间
202	- [ ] Compute: GPU 型号、训练时间、总 GPU-hours
203	- [ ] Licenses: 数据集/模型引用完整
204	- [ ] AI Assistants: 如实声明使用情况
205	- [ ] 每项认真回答（不要全写 N/A）
206	
207	### 5.8 叙事完整性
208	
209	- [ ] Conclusion 包含所有关键限定符（如 "under greedy decoding"）
210	- [ ] Abstract 与正文一致（不能一个写 "single seed" 另一个已是 "10 seeds"）
211	- [ ] 无 Appendix Version A/B 两套叙事残留
212	- [ ] 无 LaTeX 注释与正文混淆
213	- [ ] Contribution claim 在 Introduction 中（不在 Related Work 中）
214	- [ ] 所有专有名词/缩写首次出现时有定义（Abstract 内缩写也必须展开）
215	- [ ] Introduction 与 Method/Results 讲同一条主线（idea 变化后全文逻辑一致）
216	
217	### 5.9 去 AI 风格检查
218	
219	- [ ] **`grep "—" paper/*.tex` 全文清零**（解释性 em-dash 必须全删，最显著的 AI 痕迹）
220	- [ ] **`grep " – " paper/*.tex` 全文清零**（解释性 en-dash 必须全删）
221	- [ ] 无 "-ing," 分词短语结尾（如 "..., demonstrating the effectiveness of..."）
222	- [ ] 无连续 "Furthermore" / "Moreover" / "Additionally"（同段最多 1 个）
223	- [ ] 无 "It is worth noting that..." / "Notably, ..."
224	- [ ] 无 "delve into" / "leverage" / "utilize" / "a myriad of" / "a plethora of"
225	- [ ] 自然段 5-8 句是正常的，不要每 2-3 句就换段
226	
227	### 5.10 模板与同类论文核对
228	
229	- [ ] LaTeX 模板从目标会议官网下载（不是他人转载、不是上一年）
230	- [ ] `\documentclass[]{}` 选项匹配 review / camera-ready 阶段
231	- [ ] 写作前已参考 2-3 篇同领域近 1-2 年优秀论文，叙事节奏对齐
232	
233	---
234	
235	## 六、Reviewer 审查标准
236	
237	### 6.1 CRITICAL 级别（必须修复才能提交）
238	
239	- 论文数字与实验数据不一致
240	- Abstract 与正文矛盾
241	- Evaluation protocol 混淆（如 0-shot 写成 8-shot）
242	- 未经验证的数据写入论文
243	- 占位符残留
244	
245	### 6.2 WARNING 级别（应当修复）
246	
247	- Stale claims（更新了某处数字但忘了同步其他位置）
248	- 过强措辞不匹配数据支撑
249	- 隐式全因子设计误导（如写 "3×3×3=27" 但实际只有 15 格）
250	- 评估指标只描述了部分 domain
251	- 旧版数据引用
252	
253	### 6.3 数据一致性审查流程
254	
255	1. 从 registry 提取所有实验 metrics
256	2. 对照论文中每一个内联数字（到行号级别）
257	3. 独立重算所有衍生值
258	4. 不一致处标注为 CRITICAL
259	5. 近似表述检查实际比值是否在允许范围内
260	
261	---
262	
263	## 七、常见反模式速查表
264	
265	| 反模式 | 症状 | 修复方式 |
266	|--------|------|----------|
267	| Stale claim | 论文某处还引用旧数字 | 改数字后全文 grep 同步 |
268	| Protocol 混淆 | 不同表格用了不同 evaluation 但没说明 | 每张表注明 protocol |
269	| Agent 误报 | 实验结果缺乏文件证据 | 要求 `cat result.json` 截图 |
270	| 混用数据算比值 | 跨 seed/条件/N 的数据混合比较 | 只用严格配对的数据 |
271	| 叙事超越数据 | "confirmed" 但实际只是 suggestive | 匹配 claim 强度到 §2.1 |
272	| 冷引用 | 首次出现的概念无铺垫 | 先建立框架再引入 |
273	| 定义-例子矛盾 | Taxonomy 定义和示例冲突 | 审查所有定义与其示例 |
274	| Placeholder 残留 | XX.XX, TODO, [If...] 未清理 | 提交前 grep 硬门禁 |
275	| Path 泄露 | 代码/config 含服务器绝对路径 | 改为相对路径 |
276	| 重复推导 | 同一解释在 3 处各自推导一遍 | 主文一次 + 引用 Appendix |
277	| Discussion 重复 Results | Discussion 大量复制 Results 数字 | 改为引用表格编号 |
278	| 单 seed overclaim | 单 seed 数据声称 scale-invariant | 加 preliminary/hedging 限定 |
279	| Registry 不同步 | Registry 面值与实际状态不一致 | 以 SSH 实测为准 |
280	| vLLM 静默失败 | max_model_len 太小导致 100% 400 错误 | 预检必须发真实 prompt 验证 |
281	
282	---
283	
284	## 八、写论文前加载的 Skills
285	
286	写论文或做最终审查时，Director/Agent 应按需加载以下 skills：
287	- `latex-paper` — LaTeX 编译与格式
288	- `reference-audit` — 引用真实性审计
289	- `academic-writer` — ML 学术写作规范
290	- `paper-quality-lessons`（本 skill）— 实战经验教训
291	
292	---
293	
294	## 九、附录：投稿经验时间线教训
295	
296	1. **论文数字锁定时机**：最终编译前 24h 锁定所有数字，之后只允许格式修改
297	2. **GPU 不要空闲**：审稿期间如果 Agent 空闲，应该跑 ablation/扩展实验作为 rebuttal 储备
298	3. **匿名化提前做**：不要等到最后一天才检查路径泄露，fresh repo 需要时间清理
299	4. **9 页零余量策略**：NeurIPS 正文 9 页是硬限，每次新增内容必须等量压缩并编译验证
300	5. **Contingency 叙事提前写**：关键实验完成前就写好两版叙事，避免最后一刻仓促改稿
301

---

allowed-tools: [Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep]

version: 1
tags:
  - writing

---

# 论文写作质量指南（NeurIPS 实战经验）

> 来源：2026 年 NeurIPS 投稿期间，从 20+ 项目的人工审查反馈中提炼。
> 每条规则都源自真实的 bug / 退回 / 审稿质疑。

---

## 一、数据诚信与溯源（最高优先级）

### 1.1 数字必须有源头

- 论文中**每一个数字**必须可追溯到 registry 实验 ID 或原始结果文件
- 禁止凭记忆写数字——必须 `cat result.json | head` + `ls -la` 附上文件证据
- 计算值（均值、标准差、DID、delta）必须独立重算，不信 Agent 第一手汇报
- `paper_provenance.yaml` 覆盖率必须 100%，改数字必须同步更新 provenance

> **教训（D149 事件）**：Agent 曾伪造完整的 metrics 数据包括 p-value，事后被 Reviewer 独立 parse JSON 抓出。从此所有关键数据必须 Reviewer 独立验证到字段级别。

### 1.2 不同来源数据不能混用

- 配对数据必须同 seed、同 c 值、同 N、同 evaluation protocol
- 两张表如果 protocol 不同（如 0-shot vs 8-shot），论文必须明确说明
- 跨 config 比较 delta 会引入系统误差——必须补跑同 config baseline 后才能比较
- 非等量对比必须显式标注（如 "at unmatched volumes"）

> **教训（D027 事件）**：不同 config 文件的 baseline 不同，跨 config 比较 delta 值引入了 artifact。

### 1.3 结论撤回后不可复活

- 被 Director shelved 的数据（如因截断混淆），禁止重新引入论文
- `paper_provenance.yaml` 中 `verified: false` 的 claim，不得恢复
- 术语修正后不可回退（如 "same norm" → "same per-layer standard deviation"）

---

## 二、Claim 强度与数据匹配

### 2.1 Claim 强度规则

| 数据支撑 | 允许的最强表述 |
|----------|--------------|
| 单 seed, 单数据集 | "preliminary observation", "initial evidence" |
| 单 seed, 多数据集 | "suggestive pattern", "indicative trend" |
| 多 seed, 单数据集 | 报告均值±标准差，可写 "we find" |
| 多 seed, 多数据集 | 可用 "robust", "consistent" |
| 统计检验显著 | 可用 "significant", 附 p-value |
| 单 seed + 外推到其他条件 | 必须加限定，不能声称 "scale-invariant" 等 |

### 2.2 禁止的过强表述

- "remarkably stable" → 改为 "relatively stable" 或给出量化波动范围
- "confirmed" → 仅 "suggestive" 级别数据不能用
- "scale-invariant" → single-seed 验证不够
- "We attribute X to Y" → 如果是假说，必须改为 "We hypothesize" + "requiring causal verification"
- "roughly twice" → 实际比值必须在 1.8x-2.2x 才能用，否则改为更准确的近似
- "domain-agnostic" → 改为 "robust across N domains tested"

### 2.3 Claim 降级机制

当证据不足以支撑独立 claim 时，应降级为 discussion 中的定性讨论，而非删除。具体做法：
- 独立 contribution → Discussion 段落
- 硬 claim → 加 caveat 的软 claim
- 正文数字 → 移入 Appendix

---

## 三、叙事与 Storytelling

### 3.1 结构原则

- 核心 paradox/发现之间必须有**过渡句**桥接，不能让读者在关键处断线
- Introduction 每条 Contribution 必须有对应的 section/table 支撑
- Discussion 不应重复 Results 的具体数字——引用表格编号
- 同一解释不要在多处重复推导——主文写一次 + 指向 Appendix
- Limitations 段不要写成一个 17 行大段——拆分为 2-3 个子段按主题分组

### 3.2 冷引用（Cold Reference）

- 任何首次出现的概念必须有上文铺垫
- Introduction 贡献列表中不能突然出现未被提及的模型/方法名

### 3.3 不要用旧叙事套新数字

新 baseline 出来后若 delta 大幅变化，Section 的叙事逻辑必须重写，不是简单替换数字。

### 3.4 Contingency Plan

关键实验结果不确定时需预写两套叙事（如 "若结果 A → 叙事 A"、"若结果 B → 叙事 B"），实验完成后选择正确版本。提交前必须确认只留了一套。

### 3.5 不要基于中间值做叙事决策

70% 进度时的估计往往不够稳定（尤其 GSM8K 等难度分布不均匀的 benchmark），必须等完整数据再定稿叙事。

---

## 四、术语与一致性

### 4.1 术语一致性

- 全文必须统一使用正式定义的术语，不得出现同义词漂移
- 术语定义后，每次使用必须完全一致（不要有时 "perturbation sensitivity" 有时 "perturbation impact"）

### 4.2 统计量一致性

- 两个不同的 kappa/p-value 每次出现时必须标注是哪个
- 同一个 metric 在不同位置的数字必须完全一致
- 修改任何数字后必须全文 grep 确认所有引用处同步

### 4.3 p-value 格式

- 无前导零、3 位小数：`p = .003`（不是 `p = 0.003`）
- 当非劣效性 p<0.001 实际由正向效应驱动时，必须加括注说明

### 4.4 例子与定义必须一致

Taxonomy 中的定义和对应示例不能自相矛盾。如果定义说 "no new content"，示例中就不能包含新信息。

---

## 五、投稿前检查清单（Pre-Submission Checklist）

### 5.1 占位符扫描（硬门禁）

提交前必须 grep 扫描，以下模式要求**零匹配**：
```
XX.XX, PLACEHOLDER, [If , TODO, TBD, \placeholder{
```
所有条件占位段落（`[If ...]`）必须替换为最终文本。

### 5.2 编译检查

- [ ] 编译零 error
- [ ] 无 `??` 未解析引用
- [ ] 无 > 1pt 的 overfull hbox
- [ ] 正文 ≤ 9 页（NeurIPS desk reject 风险）
- [ ] 使用当年 style file（`neurips_2026.sty`）
- [ ] Review 版启用行号
- [ ] 匿名审稿版无作者姓名、无致谢

### 5.3 数据完整性

- [ ] 论文所有数字与 registry/provenance 交叉验证通过
- [ ] 计算值（均值、标准差、DID、delta）独立重算确认
- [ ] 所有 evaluation protocol 差异已在论文中说明
- [ ] 多 seed 结果报告均值和标准差
- [ ] 单 seed 数据在 Limitations 中声明

### 5.4 图表检查

- [ ] 所有 figure PDF 存在且路径匹配
- [ ] 图表不超栏宽（单栏 5.5in / 全宽 6.5in）
- [ ] 图中字体 ≥ 7pt
- [ ] 小数精度全表统一
- [ ] 最优结果加粗、次优下划线
- [ ] 表格标题（caption）自包含
- [ ] Forest plot 等可视化无 dummy 值（CI_LO=-99 等）

### 5.5 引用检查

- [ ] 引用覆盖：**直接相关方法、baseline 论文、评测 benchmark 论文、理论基础**（任一缺失说明调研不充分）
- [ ] 引用密度与目标会议近年录用论文同量级
- [ ] 引用键与 bib 条目 1:1 匹配
- [ ] 无孤儿 bib 条目
- [ ] 无幻觉引用（所有被引论文实际存在）
- [ ] 近年论文的年份/会议准确
- [ ] 审稿人要求的引用全部补齐

### 5.6 匿名化检查

- [ ] 源代码无硬编码绝对路径（`/Users/...`, `/root/...`）
- [ ] 配置文件无服务器路径
- [ ] Git history 已清理 author 信息（用 fresh repo）
- [ ] 项目管理文件不得提交（AGENTS.md, memory.md, registry.yaml, task_context/ 等）
- [ ] API Keys 通过环境变量，无泄露

### 5.7 会议 Checklist 填写（如目标会议要求）

- [ ] Claims: 摘要/Introduction 准确反映实验范围
- [ ] Limitations: 正文 Limitations 段 + Appendix 补充
- [ ] Experiments: 实验设置完整（exp_id, seed, 超参, 评估 protocol）
- [ ] Reproducibility: 数据集公开、代码可用
- [ ] Statistical Significance: 多 seed 均值+标准差、置信区间
- [ ] Compute: GPU 型号、训练时间、总 GPU-hours
- [ ] Licenses: 数据集/模型引用完整
- [ ] AI Assistants: 如实声明使用情况
- [ ] 每项认真回答（不要全写 N/A）

### 5.8 叙事完整性

- [ ] Conclusion 包含所有关键限定符（如 "under greedy decoding"）
- [ ] Abstract 与正文一致（不能一个写 "single seed" 另一个已是 "10 seeds"）
- [ ] 无 Appendix Version A/B 两套叙事残留
- [ ] 无 LaTeX 注释与正文混淆
- [ ] Contribution claim 在 Introduction 中（不在 Related Work 中）
- [ ] 所有专有名词/缩写首次出现时有定义（Abstract 内缩写也必须展开）
- [ ] Introduction 与 Method/Results 讲同一条主线（idea 变化后全文逻辑一致）

### 5.9 去 AI 风格检查

- [ ] **`grep "—" paper/*.tex` 全文清零**（解释性 em-dash 必须全删，最显著的 AI 痕迹）
- [ ] **`grep " – " paper/*.tex` 全文清零**（解释性 en-dash 必须全删）
- [ ] 无 "-ing," 分词短语结尾（如 "..., demonstrating the effectiveness of..."）
- [ ] 无连续 "Furthermore" / "Moreover" / "Additionally"（同段最多 1 个）
- [ ] 无 "It is worth noting that..." / "Notably, ..."
- [ ] 无 "delve into" / "leverage" / "utilize" / "a myriad of" / "a plethora of"
- [ ] 自然段 5-8 句是正常的，不要每 2-3 句就换段

### 5.10 模板与同类论文核对

- [ ] LaTeX 模板从目标会议官网下载（不是他人转载、不是上一年）
- [ ] `\documentclass[]{}` 选项匹配 review / camera-ready 阶段
- [ ] 写作前已参考 2-3 篇同领域近 1-2 年优秀论文，叙事节奏对齐

---

## 六、Reviewer 审查标准

### 6.1 CRITICAL 级别（必须修复才能提交）

- 论文数字与实验数据不一致
- Abstract 与正文矛盾
- Evaluation protocol 混淆（如 0-shot 写成 8-shot）
- 未经验证的数据写入论文
- 占位符残留

### 6.2 WARNING 级别（应当修复）

- Stale claims（更新了某处数字但忘了同步其他位置）
- 过强措辞不匹配数据支撑
- 隐式全因子设计误导（如写 "3×3×3=27" 但实际只有 15 格）
- 评估指标只描述了部分 domain
- 旧版数据引用

### 6.3 数据一致性审查流程

1. 从 registry 提取所有实验 metrics
2. 对照论文中每一个内联数字（到行号级别）
3. 独立重算所有衍生值
4. 不一致处标注为 CRITICAL
5. 近似表述检查实际比值是否在允许范围内

---

## 七、常见反模式速查表

| 反模式 | 症状 | 修复方式 |
|--------|------|----------|
| Stale claim | 论文某处还引用旧数字 | 改数字后全文 grep 同步 |
| Protocol 混淆 | 不同表格用了不同 evaluation 但没说明 | 每张表注明 protocol |

1	\section{EC-HTE: Error-Corrected Heterogeneous Treatment Effects}
2	\label{sec:method}
3	
4	EC-HTE corrects subgroup-level misclassification bias in three stages: estimate per-subgroup confusion matrices via hierarchical Bayes, invert them to correct observed outcome moments, and propagate correction uncertainty into downstream causal estimators.
5	
6	\subsection{Hierarchical Bayes Confusion Matrix Estimation}
7	
8	We place a Dirichlet-Multinomial hierarchical model over the confusion matrices $\{C_s\}_{s=1}^K$.
9	For each subgroup $s$, row $j$ of $C_s$ has a Dirichlet prior $\text{Dir}(\alpha_0 \cdot \mathbf{e}_j)$, where $\mathbf{e}_j$ is the $j$-th standard basis vector and $\alpha_0 > 0$ is a shared concentration parameter.
10	A $\text{Gamma}(3, 1)$ hyperprior on $\alpha_0$ controls the strength of partial pooling across subgroups: large $\alpha_0$ pulls subgroup estimates toward the identity matrix (low error), while small $\alpha_0$ allows subgroup-specific rates to dominate.
11	This partial pooling implements a James-Stein shrinkage effect, borrowing strength across subgroups to reduce variance for small subgroups while preserving heterogeneity where the data support it.
12	
13	Posterior inference uses a Gibbs sampler with 4 chains, 4000 iterations (2000 warmup).
14	We require convergence diagnostics $\hat{R} < 1.01$ and effective sample size $\text{ESS} > 845$ for all parameters before accepting estimates.
15	In practice, all runs achieve $\hat{R} < 1.0034$ and $\text{ESS} > 1618$, well within these thresholds.
16	HB estimation outperforms stratified MLE in 87.5\% of configurations (21 of 24) across the experimental grid (Section~\ref{sec:ec_hte_eval}), with the largest gains when $n_{\text{expert}} / K < 100$.
17	The advantage requires at least $n_{\text{expert}} / K \geq 25$ per subgroup; below this threshold, stratified MLE is preferred because the hierarchical model lacks sufficient observations for stable shrinkage.
18	At $n_{\text{expert}} \geq 1000$, HB and stratified MLE converge to within 0.5\% on all metrics.
19	Sensitivity analysis shows $<$5\% RMSE variation under 2$\times$ hyperprior perturbation, confirming that results are not driven by prior specification.
20	
21	\subsection{Subgroup-Stratified Correction}
22	
23	Given posterior mean confusion matrices $\hat{C}_s$, we correct observed outcome moments per subgroup by matrix inversion:
24	\begin{equation}
25	\tilde{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_s = \hat{C}_s^{-1} \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_s,
26	\end{equation}
27	where $\hat{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_s = [\hat{\tau}_{\text{obs}}(0, s),\, \hat{\tau}_{\text{obs}}(1, s)]^\top$ collects the observed conditional outcome moments in subgroup $s$.
28	This requires $\det(\hat{C}_s) \neq 0$ for all $s$, which holds under assumption~(A4) ($\pi_s \neq 0.5$) but may fail in finite samples when error rates approach degeneracy.
29	In practice, Laplace smoothing of the confusion matrix counts ensures finite-sample invertibility.
30	We impose a singularity guard: if the condition number $\kappa(\hat{C}_s) > 100$, subgroup $s$ falls back to global correction $\bar{C}^{-1}$ rather than risk numerical instability from near-singular inversion.
31	
32	The contrast with global correction is direct.
33	Global correction applies $\bar{C}^{-1}$ uniformly to all subgroups, introducing the $\delta_s \cdot \Delta\tau$ bias identified in Theorem~\ref{thm:bias_identity}.
34	Subgroup-stratified correction eliminates this bias by matching each subgroup's correction to its own misclassification structure, at the cost of higher variance from estimating $K$ separate confusion matrices (Section~\ref{sec:budget}).
35	
36	\subsection{Variance-Adjusted CausalForest}
37	
38	For heterogeneous treatment effect estimation, we feed corrected covariates into CausalForestDML~\cite{wager2018causal} with honest splitting.
39	The forest produces per-observation standard error estimates $\text{se}_i$.
40	To account for confusion matrix correction, we propagate uncertainty through the inverse mapping:
41	\begin{equation}
42	\text{se}_{\text{corrected},i} = \sqrt{\text{diag}\!\left(\hat{C}_{S_i}^{-1}\, \text{diag}(\text{se}_i^2)\, \hat{C}_{S_i}^{-\top}\right)}.
43	\end{equation}
44	This is a plug-in approach: the standard errors reflect outcome variance conditional on $\hat{C}_s$ but do not propagate uncertainty from the confusion matrix estimation itself.
45	At $n_{\text{expert}} \geq 100$, the plug-in approximation is reasonable because confusion matrix estimation variance is small relative to outcome variance.
46	Below this threshold, the standard errors may understate total uncertainty; this limitation is discussed further in the Limitations section.
47	
48	\paragraph{Diagnostic criterion.}
49	As a practical corollary of Theorem~\ref{thm:bias_identity}, the product $|\Delta\pi \times \Delta\tau|$ serves as a computable diagnostic for whether global correction will harm specific subgroups.
50	The bias decomposition identity predicts that bias is proportional to this product, and both quantities can be estimated from a modest pilot sample (we use $n_{\text{expert}} = 50$ in our experiments).
51	A threshold calibrated via leave-one-out cross-validation achieves AUC~=~0.833 at the subgroup level (Section~\ref{sec:diagnostic}).
52	The recommended workflow is: compute the diagnostic from pilot data; if any subgroup shows a large product, apply EC-HTE; if the product is uniformly small, global correction suffices.
53	
54	\paragraph{Composition with PPCI.}
55	EC-HTE corrects structured covariate misclassification through $\hat{C}_s^{-1}$ inversion but cannot address outcome-level measurement error.
56	PPCI~\cite{sui2026ppci} corrects residual outcome bias using a debiasing estimator but assumes correct covariate labels.
57	The two methods are complementary: apply EC-HTE first to correct covariate labels, then PPCI to correct outcome predictions.
58	Neither is redundant with the other: EC-HTE alone cannot fix outcome error, while PPCI alone incurs higher variance for covariate error.
59	Under both error types simultaneously, the composition reduces $|\text{bias}|$ from 0.179 to below 0.01 (Section~\ref{sec:ppci}).

\section{EC-HTE: Error-Corrected Heterogeneous Treatment Effects}
\label{sec:method}

EC-HTE corrects subgroup-level misclassification bias in three stages: estimate per-subgroup confusion matrices via hierarchical Bayes, invert them to correct observed outcome moments, and propagate correction uncertainty into downstream causal estimators.

\subsection{Hierarchical Bayes Confusion Matrix Estimation}

We place a Dirichlet-Multinomial hierarchical model over the confusion matrices $\{C_s\}_{s=1}^K$.
For each subgroup $s$, row $j$ of $C_s$ has a Dirichlet prior $\text{Dir}(\alpha_0 \cdot \mathbf{e}_j)$, where $\mathbf{e}_j$ is the $j$-th standard basis vector and $\alpha_0 > 0$ is a shared concentration parameter.
A $\text{Gamma}(3, 1)$ hyperprior on $\alpha_0$ controls the strength of partial pooling across subgroups: large $\alpha_0$ pulls subgroup estimates toward the identity matrix (low error), while small $\alpha_0$ allows subgroup-specific rates to dominate.
This partial pooling implements a James-Stein shrinkage effect, borrowing strength across subgroups to reduce variance for small subgroups while preserving heterogeneity where the data support it.

Posterior inference uses a Gibbs sampler with 4 chains, 4000 iterations (2000 warmup).
We require convergence diagnostics $\hat{R} < 1.01$ and effective sample size $\text{ESS} > 845$ for all parameters before accepting estimates.
In practice, all runs achieve $\hat{R} < 1.0034$ and $\text{ESS} > 1618$, well within these thresholds.
HB estimation outperforms stratified MLE in 87.5\% of configurations (21 of 24) across the experimental grid (Section~\ref{sec:ec_hte_eval}), with the largest gains when $n_{\text{expert}} / K < 100$.
The advantage requires at least $n_{\text{expert}} / K \geq 25$ per subgroup; below this threshold, stratified MLE is preferred because the hierarchical model lacks sufficient observations for stable shrinkage.
At $n_{\text{expert}} \geq 1000$, HB and stratified MLE converge to within 0.5\% on all metrics.
Sensitivity analysis shows $<$5\% RMSE variation under 2$\times$ hyperprior perturbation, confirming that results are not driven by prior specification.

\subsection{Subgroup-Stratified Correction}

Given posterior mean confusion matrices $\hat{C}_s$, we correct observed outcome moments per subgroup by matrix inversion:
\begin{equation}
\tilde{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_s = \hat{C}_s^{-1} \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_s,
\end{equation}
where $\hat{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_s = [\hat{\tau}_{\text{obs}}(0, s),\, \hat{\tau}_{\text{obs}}(1, s)]^\top$ collects the observed conditional outcome moments in subgroup $s$.
This requires $\det(\hat{C}_s) \neq 0$ for all $s$, which holds under assumption~(A4) ($\pi_s \neq 0.5$) but may fail in finite samples when error rates approach degeneracy.
In practice, Laplace smoothing of the confusion matrix counts ensures finite-sample invertibility.
We impose a singularity guard: if the condition number $\kappa(\hat{C}_s) > 100$, subgroup $s$ falls back to global correction $\bar{C}^{-1}$ rather than risk numerical instability from near-singular inversion.

The contrast with global correction is direct.
Global correction applies $\bar{C}^{-1}$ uniformly to all subgroups, introducing the $\delta_s \cdot \Delta\tau$ bias identified in Theorem~\ref{thm:bias_identity}.
Subgroup-stratified correction eliminates this bias by matching each subgroup's correction to its own misclassification structure, at the cost of higher variance from estimating $K$ separate confusion matrices (Section~\ref{sec:budget}).

\subsection{Variance-Adjusted CausalForest}

For heterogeneous treatment effect estimation, we feed corrected covariates into CausalForestDML~\cite{wager2018causal} with honest splitting.
The forest produces per-observation standard error estimates $\text{se}_i$.
To account for confusion matrix correction, we propagate uncertainty through the inverse mapping:
\begin{equation}
\text{se}_{\text{corrected},i} = \sqrt{\text{diag}\!\left(\hat{C}_{S_i}^{-1}\, \text{diag}(\text{se}_i^2)\, \hat{C}_{S_i}^{-\top}\right)}.
\end{equation}
This is a plug-in approach: the standard errors reflect outcome variance conditional on $\hat{C}_s$ but do not propagate uncertainty from the confusion matrix estimation itself.
At $n_{\text{expert}} \geq 100$, the plug-in approximation is reasonable because confusion matrix estimation variance is small relative to outcome variance.
Below this threshold, the standard errors may understate total uncertainty; this limitation is discussed further in the Limitations section.

\paragraph{Diagnostic criterion.}
As a practical corollary of Theorem~\ref{thm:bias_identity}, the product $|\Delta\pi \times \Delta\tau|$ serves as a computable diagnostic for whether global correction will harm specific subgroups.
The bias decomposition identity predicts that bias is proportional to this product, and both quantities can be estimated from a modest pilot sample (we use $n_{\text{expert}} = 50$ in our experiments).
A threshold calibrated via leave-one-out cross-validation achieves AUC~=~0.833 at the subgroup level (Section~\ref{sec:diagnostic}).
The recommended workflow is: compute the diagnostic from pilot data; if any subgroup shows a large product, apply EC-HTE; if the product is uniformly small, global correction suffices.

\paragraph{Composition with PPCI.}
EC-HTE corrects structured covariate misclassification through $\hat{C}_s^{-1}$ inversion but cannot address outcome-level measurement error.
PPCI~\cite{sui2026ppci} corrects residual outcome bias using a debiasing estimator but assumes correct covariate labels.
The two methods are complementary: apply EC-HTE first to correct covariate labels, then PPCI to correct outcome predictions.
Neither is redundant with the other: EC-HTE alone cannot fix outcome error, while PPCI alone incurs higher variance for covariate error.
Under both error types simultaneously, the composition reduces $|\text{bias}|$ from 0.179 to below 0.01 (Section~\ref{sec:ppci}).

\begin{abstract}
Large language model (LLM) annotations increasingly serve as effect modifiers in computational social science analyses of heterogeneous treatment effects (HTEs), yet misclassification rates vary systematically across demographic subgroups.
Standard practice corrects for annotation error using a single pooled confusion matrix, implicitly assuming homogeneous error rates.
We prove a bias decomposition identity showing that global correction introduces bias exactly proportional to the product of misclassification heterogeneity and conditional average treatment effect (CATE) heterogeneity ($\Delta\pi \times \Delta\tau$), an exact population-level result verified at $R^2 = 0.994$ ($K{=}2$).
In 50\% of experimental configurations, global correction worsens subgroup CATE bias, with amplification up to 2.86$\times$ ($K{=}2$, difference-in-means) and 5.9$\times$ ($K{=}4$, CausalForest).
Error-Corrected Heterogeneous Treatment Effects (EC-HTE) combines hierarchical Bayesian subgroup-stratified confusion matrix estimation with CausalForestDML, reducing $|\text{bias}|$ from 0.059 to 0.011 under extreme heterogeneity ($K{=}2$); a computable diagnostic ($\Delta\pi \times \Delta\tau$ product, AUC $= 0.833$) identifies when stratified correction is warranted.
Composed with Prediction-Powered Conditional Inference (PPCI) for dual covariate/outcome error, the two corrections are each necessary and jointly sufficient, reducing $|\text{bias}|$ from 0.179 to 0.007.
EC-HTE's advantage is conditional on sufficient error heterogeneity; when $\Delta\pi$ is small, global correction suffices.
We validate across 520 synthetic configurations (100 Monte Carlo runs each) and a semi-synthetic TweetEval experiment ($N{=}5{,}000$).
\end{abstract}

1	\section{Related Work}
2	\label{sec:related}
3	
4	\paragraph{Measurement error in regression and causal models.}
5	The classical measurement error literature establishes that naive regression with mismeasured covariates yields attenuated coefficient estimates, and that correction via estimated error models can amplify mean squared error when the error structure is misspecified~\cite{fuller1987measurement,carroll2006measurement}.
6	Bayesian treatments model the measurement process jointly with the outcome, requiring informative priors when identification is weak~\cite{gustafson2003measurement}.
7	Nonparametric identification results show that repeated measurements or instrumental variables can recover the true distribution without parametric assumptions on the error mechanism~\cite{hu2008nonparametric}.

\section{Related Work}
\label{sec:related}

\paragraph{Measurement error in regression and causal models.}
The classical measurement error literature establishes that naive regression with mismeasured covariates yields attenuated coefficient estimates, and that correction via estimated error models can amplify mean squared error when the error structure is misspecified~\cite{fuller1987measurement,carroll2006measurement}.
Bayesian treatments model the measurement process jointly with the outcome, requiring informative priors when identification is weak~\cite{gustafson2003measurement}.
Nonparametric identification results show that repeated measurements or instrumental variables can recover the true distribution without parametric assumptions on the error mechanism~\cite{hu2008nonparametric}.
A recurring theme is that correction helps only when the error model is well-specified; misspecified correction can perform worse than ignoring the error entirely.
We formalize this principle for a specific causal estimand: Theorem~\ref{thm:bias_identity} gives an exact identity for CATE bias under global correction with heterogeneous misclassification rates, and derives the condition under which global correction amplifies rather than reduces bias.

\paragraph{Bayesian annotation models.}
\citet{dawid1979maximum} introduced confusion matrix estimation for multiple annotators via EM, enabling label aggregation that accounts for annotator reliability.
Extensions incorporate item difficulty~\cite{passonneau2014benefits}, learned annotator competence~\cite{hovy2013learning}, and hierarchical priors that share information across annotators with varying expertise~\cite{paun2018comparing}.
These models target label quality for classification tasks.
Our hierarchical confusion matrix estimator (Section~\ref{sec:method}) adapts this architecture to causal inference: the estimated subgroup-stratified matrices feed into CATE correction rather than label aggregation, and the prior structure is tied to the subgroup dimension that defines treatment effect heterogeneity.

\paragraph{Heterogeneous treatment effect estimation.}
Causal forests recursively partition the covariate space to estimate conditional treatment effects with valid confidence intervals~\cite{athey2016recursive,wager2018causal}.
Double/debiased machine learning provides Neyman-orthogonal moment conditions that yield root-$n$ consistent estimates robust to slow first-stage convergence~\cite{chernozhukov2018dml}.
Doubly-robust CATE estimators achieve minimax rates under flexible nuisance estimation~\cite{kennedy2023dr}, and meta-learners unify several approaches within a common framework~\cite{kunzel2019metalearners}.
These methods all assume that the covariates defining heterogeneity are observed without error.
When the effect modifier is misclassified, the heterogeneity structure itself is distorted: observations are assigned to wrong subgroups, and the resulting CATE estimates conflate effects across groups.
EC-HTE provides upstream correction that restores valid inputs to any of these downstream estimators (Section~\ref{sec:method}).

\paragraph{LLMs as annotators.}
LLMs now match or exceed crowd-worker accuracy on many text classification tasks~\cite{gilardi2023chatgpt,tornberg2024chatgpt}, and surveys document their expanding role across computational social science~\cite{ziems2024nlp,pangakis2023automated}.
However, error rates are not uniform.
\citet{ashwin2025bias} show that misclassification varies by up to $5\times$ across demographic subgroups defined by refugee status, gender, and education.
This heterogeneity is precisely the failure mode we address: when subgroup-varying LLM errors feed into HTE analysis, they distort the very contrasts that define the research question.
Prior work documents these error patterns but provides no correction mechanism for downstream causal estimands.

\paragraph{Prediction-powered and design-based correction.}
Prediction-Powered Inference (PPI) constructs valid confidence intervals for population parameters by combining a large set of ML predictions with a small gold-standard sample~\cite{angelopoulos2023ppi}, with extensions to cross-prediction and active sampling~\cite{zrnic2024cross}.
Design-based Supervised Learning (DSL) achieves similar goals through a survey-sampling framework~\cite{egami2024dsl}; applied per-subgroup, DSL can correct subgroup estimates but operates at the estimand level (adjusting observed statistics directly) without cross-subgroup borrowing, resulting in strictly higher variance than EC-HTE's measurement-model approach (confusion matrix inversion with hierarchical shrinkage).
\citet{mozer2026ppi} extend PPI to arm-specific correction for average treatment effects under differential prediction error.
PPCI~\cite{sui2026ppci} targets conditional estimands but corrects outcome-side prediction error ($\hat{Y}$ given true $Z$), not covariate-side misclassification.
ForestIV~\cite{bu2023forestiv} instruments for ML-predicted covariates in regression forests but targets the outcome model rather than the heterogeneity structure.
\citet{grimmer2022text} and \citet{audinet2025benchmarking} provide broader methodological guidance for text-as-data pipelines without specific correction for causal heterogeneity.
All of these methods address either population-level correction or outcome-side error; none corrects the case where the mismeasured variable is the effect modifier whose levels index the CATE function.

\citet{imai2010causal} study misclassification of the \textit{treatment variable}, where errors change which arm a unit is assigned to.
Their setting requires instrumental variables or partial identification bounds because treatment misclassification directly compromises the identification of average effects.
Our problem is structurally distinct: the treatment is observed correctly, but the \textit{effect modifier} that defines subgroups is misclassified.
This does not threaten ATE identification but distorts the heterogeneity structure, a bias that admits exact correction through subgroup-stratified confusion matrices rather than bounds.
The two problems share surface similarity (both involve misclassification in causal inference) but differ in which dimension is corrupted, what estimand is affected, and what correction is feasible.

1	% Requires preamble: \usepackage{amsthm,amsmath,amssymb}
2	% and: \newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}
3	%      \newtheorem{corollary}[theorem]{Corollary}
4	%      \newtheorem{proposition}[theorem]{Proposition}
5	
6	\section{Bias Decomposition: When Debiasing Hurts}
7	\label{sec:theory}
8	
9	We formalize the bias that global misclassification correction introduces when subgroup error rates are heterogeneous.
10	Consider estimating the conditional average treatment effect (CATE) $\tau(z) = \mathbb{E}[Y(1) - Y(0) \mid Z = z]$, where $Z \in \{0, 1\}$ is a binary effect modifier observed only through a noisy annotation $\hat{Z}$.
11	The population consists of $K$ subgroups $S \in \{1, \ldots, K\}$ with weights $w_s = P(S{=}s)$, each characterized by a $2 \times 2$ confusion matrix $C_s$ with symmetric error rate $\pi_s = P(\hat{Z} \neq Z \mid S{=}s)$.
12	Standard practice estimates a single confusion matrix $\bar{C} = \sum_s w_s C_s$ from expert annotations and applies its inverse uniformly to all observations, with pooled error rate $\bar{\pi} = \sum_s w_s \pi_s$.
13	We show that when error rates vary across subgroups, this global procedure introduces a bias with an exact product form.
14	
15	We state four assumptions maintained throughout.
16	%
17	\begin{itemize}
18	\item[\textbf{(A1)}] \textit{Conditional independence:} misclassification depends only on the true label $Z$ and subgroup $S$, not on potential outcomes $Y(0), Y(1)$.
19	\item[\textbf{(A2)}] \textit{Symmetric misclassification:} $P(\hat{Z}{=}1 \mid Z{=}0, S{=}s) = P(\hat{Z}{=}0 \mid Z{=}1, S{=}s) = \pi_s$ for all $s$.
20	\item[\textbf{(A3)}] \textit{Balanced effect modifier:} $P(Z{=}0) = P(Z{=}1) = 0.5$. This simplifies the exposition; we discuss relaxation below.
21	\item[\textbf{(A4)}] \textit{Non-degeneracy:} $\pi_s \neq 0.5$ for all $s$, ensuring each $C_s$ is invertible.
22	\end{itemize}
23	
24	Under (A2)--(A3), the Bayesian mixing matrix $M_s$ (entries $M_s[\hat{z}, z] = P(Z{=}z \mid \hat{Z}{=}\hat{z}, S{=}s)$) coincides with $C_s$.
25	The global mixing matrix is $M_{\text{global}} = \sum_s w_s M_s$.
26	
27	\begin{theorem}[Bias Decomposition Identity]
28	\label{thm:bias_identity}
29	Under \textnormal{(A1)--(A4)}, the bias of global correction in subgroup $s$ at effect-modifier level $z$ is
30	\begin{align}
31	\mathrm{bias}_{\mathrm{global}}(z{=}0, s) &= +\frac{\delta_s \cdot \Delta\tau}{1 - 2\bar{\pi}}, \label{eq:bias_z0} \\
32	\mathrm{bias}_{\mathrm{global}}(z{=}1, s) &= -\frac{\delta_s \cdot \Delta\tau}{1 - 2\bar{\pi}}, \label{eq:bias_z1}
33	\end{align}
34	where $\delta_s = \pi_s - \bar{\pi}$ is the subgroup deviation from the pooled error rate and $\Delta\tau = \tau(1) - \tau(0)$ is the CATE heterogeneity.
35	\end{theorem}
36	
37	Equations~\eqref{eq:bias_z0}--\eqref{eq:bias_z1} constitute an exact identity at the population level, not a bound.
38	The bias factors into three interpretable components: $\delta_s$ captures how much subgroup $s$ deviates from the average misclassification rate, $\Delta\tau$ captures treatment effect heterogeneity across levels of $Z$, and $1/(1 - 2\bar{\pi})$ is an amplification factor from matrix inversion.
39	Bias vanishes when either source of variation is absent ($\delta_s = 0$ or $\Delta\tau = 0$), and arises only through their interaction.
40	Theorem~\ref{thm:bias_identity} implies that global correction trades one source of confounding for another: it removes attenuation from label noise but introduces a new bias from error-rate heterogeneity.
41	
42	\paragraph{Proof sketch.}
43	Global correction applies $M_{\text{global}}^{-1}$ to the subgroup-specific observed CATE $\tau_{\text{obs}}(\cdot, s) = M_s \cdot \tau_{\text{true}}$, yielding bias $(M_{\text{global}}^{-1} M_s - I) \cdot \tau_{\text{true}}$.
44	Direct computation shows $M_{\text{global}}^{-1} M_s - I = \frac{\delta_s}{1-2\bar{\pi}} \bigl[\begin{smallmatrix} -1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 \end{smallmatrix}\bigr]$.
45	Applying this matrix to $[\tau(0),\, \tau(1)]^\top$ produces the product form.
46	The full derivation appears in Appendix~\ref{app:derivation}.
47	
48	\begin{corollary}[Multi-class Extension]
49	\label{cor:multiclass}
50	For $K > 2$ subgroups with $J$ effect-modifier levels, the subgroup bias of global correction generalizes to
51	\begin{equation}
52	\mathrm{bias}_{\mathrm{global}}(z, s) = \sum_{j=1}^{J} \bigl(\bar{\pi}_j - \pi_{s,j}\bigr) \cdot \bigl(\tau(j) - \bar{\tau}\bigr) \cdot g(\bar{\pi}),
53	\label{eq:multiclass}
54	\end{equation}
55	where $g(\bar{\pi})$ collects the matrix-inversion amplification terms.
56	The essential structure, $\sum_s w_s (\bar{\pi}_j - \pi_{s,j}) = 0$, ensures that bias redistributes across subgroups rather than vanishing in aggregate.
57	\end{corollary}
58	
59	Assumption~(A3) ensures $M_s = C_s$; when $P(Z{=}1) \neq 0.5$, the mixing matrices acquire asymmetric entries, but the product structure persists with modified coefficients (Appendix~\ref{app:derivation}).
60	Empirical verification (Section~\ref{sec:bias_mechanism}) yields $R^2 = 0.994$ for $K{=}2$ and $R^2 = 0.974$ for $K{=}4$; the residual variance reflects finite-sample Monte Carlo noise, not model misspecification.
61	
62	\paragraph{Finite-sample remainder.}
63	Theorem~\ref{thm:bias_identity} is an exact population identity.
64	In practice, confusion matrices are estimated from $n_{\text{expert}}$ expert labels, introducing an estimation error $\hat{C}_s = C_s + E_s$ where $\|E_s\| = O_p(n_{\text{expert}}^{-1/2})$.
65	The resulting remainder term in the corrected CATE is $R_n = O_p(n_{\text{expert}}^{-1/2} \cdot \kappa(C_s))$, where $\kappa(C_s)$ is the condition number of the subgroup confusion matrix.
66	This dependence on both sample size and matrix conditioning motivates the singularity guard ($\kappa > 100 \to$ fallback) described in Section~\ref{sec:method}.
67	
68	\begin{proposition}[Debiasing Can Increase Bias]
69	\label{prop:debiasing_hurts}
70	Under \textnormal{(A1)--(A4)}, global correction produces larger absolute bias than the naive estimator ($|\mathrm{bias}_{\mathrm{global}}| > |\mathrm{bias}_{\mathrm{naive}}|$) in subgroup $s$ if and only if
71	\begin{equation}
72	\frac{|\delta_s|}{(1 - 2\bar{\pi}) \cdot \pi_s} > 1.
73	\label{eq:hurts_condition}
74	\end{equation}
75	\end{proposition}
76	
77	Equation~\eqref{eq:hurts_condition} partitions subgroups into two regimes.
78	For high-error subgroups ($\pi_s > \bar{\pi}$), the condition reduces to $\pi_s > 0.5$, which is excluded by~(A4); global correction always reduces bias in these subgroups.
79	For low-error subgroups ($\pi_s < \bar{\pi}$), the condition holds whenever $\pi_s < \bar{\pi} / (2(1 - \bar{\pi}))$.
80	This threshold is easily satisfied in practice: when $\bar{\pi} = 0.15$, any subgroup with $\pi_s < 0.088$ experiences increased bias from global correction.
81	The mechanism is that global correction inverts the pooled confusion matrix, applying a correction calibrated for the average error rate; high-error subgroups are under-corrected (bias reduced but not eliminated), while low-error subgroups are over-corrected (the correction overshoots and reverses the sign of bias).
82	For subgroups with near-zero misclassification ($\pi_s \approx 0$), the naive estimator is nearly unbiased, yet global correction creates substantial bias where none existed.
83	This is the most consequential implication of Theorem~\ref{thm:bias_identity}: debiasing can be worse than doing nothing.
84	
85	In our experiments (Section~\ref{sec:bias_mechanism}), global correction increases bias in 50\% of parameter configurations (260 of 520, excluding cases where $\Delta_c{=}0$).
86	With the difference-in-means estimator, maximum amplification reaches $2.86\times$ for $K{=}2$ and $2.41\times$ for $K{=}4$; the mechanism operates across estimator types, with nonlinear estimators amplifying the effect further (Section~\ref{sec:ec_hte_eval}).
87	Figure~\ref{fig:heatmap} visualizes the amplification across the full $\Delta\pi \times \Delta\tau$ parameter grid.

1	\section{Experiments}
2	
3	\subsection{Experimental Setup and Data Generation}
4	
5	\subsubsection{Synthetic DGP}
6	
7	We generate data from a controlled data-generating process (DGP) that separates the effect of subgroup-level misclassification heterogeneity from other confounders.
8	For each observation $i$, the potential outcome under treatment $t$ is
9	\begin{equation}
10	Y_i(t) = \alpha + \tau(Z_i) \cdot t + \beta X_i + \varepsilon_i, \quad \varepsilon_i \sim \mathcal{N}(0,1),
11	\end{equation}
12	where $T_i \sim \text{Bernoulli}(0.5)$ simulates a randomized controlled trial, and $Z_i \in \{0, \ldots, K{-}1\}$ is the true effect modifier with $K \in \{2, 4\}$ subgroups.
13	The conditional average treatment effect (CATE) $\tau(Z{=}z)$ varies across subgroups with controlled heterogeneity $\Delta\tau = \max_z \tau(z) - \min_z \tau(z)$.
14	Misclassification is injected through subgroup-specific symmetric confusion matrices $C_s$: the observed label $\hat{Z}_i$ is drawn as $\hat{Z}_i \sim \text{Multinomial}(C_{S_i})$, where each subgroup $s$ has error rate $\pi_s$ and $\Delta\pi = \max_s \pi_s - \min_s \pi_s$ controls heterogeneity.
15	We fix $N{=}5000$ observations and vary $n_{\text{expert}} \in \{50, 100, 250, 500, 1000, 2000\}$ (the number of expert-labeled observations used to estimate confusion matrices).
16	Each configuration is repeated for 100 Monte Carlo runs.
17	
18	\subsubsection{Semi-synthetic DGP (TweetEval)}
19	
20	To test EC-HTE under realistic conditions, we construct a semi-synthetic DGP from the TweetEval sentiment corpus~\cite{barbieri2020tweeteval}, sampling $N{=}5000$ tweets per run from a pool of 57{,}899.
21	Four subgroups are defined by crossing two binary text features: presence of hashtags (\texttt{has\_hashtag}) and text length relative to the median (\texttt{text\_length\_bin}).
22	This yields unbalanced subgroup proportions (S0: 39\%, S1: 38\%, S2: 12\%, S3: 11\%).
23	The effect modifier is $Z{=}1$ if the true sentiment is positive ($P(Z{=}1) \approx 35\%$), and $Z{=}0$ otherwise.
24	We set subgroup-specific misclassification rates $\pi_{S0}{=}0.05$, $\pi_{S1}{=}0.10$, $\pi_{S2}{=}0.15$, $\pi_{S3}{=}0.25$ in the extreme regime, reflecting empirical evidence that hashtag-heavy text degrades LLM classifier accuracy~\cite{ashwin2025bias}.
25	The outcome model is
26	\begin{equation}
27	Y_i = 1.0 + \tau(Z_i, S_i) \cdot T_i + 0.3 \cdot \text{len}_i + 0.2 \cdot \text{mention}_i + \varepsilon_i,
28	\end{equation}
29	where $\tau(Z{=}1, S) \in \{0.5, 0.4, 0.3, 0.2\}$ for S0--S3 and $\tau(Z{=}0) = 0.1$ is the baseline effect.
30	
31	\paragraph{Baselines and metrics.}
32	We compare: (1) \textit{Naive} (no correction), (2) \textit{Global} (pooled confusion matrix), (3) \textit{Stratified MLE} (per-subgroup MLE without pooling), (4) \textit{HB EC-HTE} (our hierarchical Bayes estimator), (5) \textit{PPCI}~\cite{sui2026ppci}, and (6) \textit{EC-HTE+PPCI} (our combined method).
33	For the CausalForest estimator~\cite{wager2018causal}, we also compare naive, global, and EC-HTE variants.
34	Primary metrics are absolute bias $|\text{bias}|$, root mean squared error (RMSE), and 95\% confidence interval coverage, all averaged across subgroups and 100 MC runs.
35	
36	\subsection{Bias Mechanism Verification}
37	\label{sec:bias_mechanism}
38	
39	The bias decomposition identity (Theorem~\ref{thm:bias_identity}) predicts that global correction introduces bias proportional to $\Delta\pi \times \Delta\tau$ at the subgroup level.
40	We verify this identity empirically across 520 configurations spanning $K \in \{2,4\}$, two misclassification regimes, and six expert budget levels.
41	Regressing observed subgroup bias on the predicted $\Delta\pi \times \Delta\tau$ product yields $R^2 = 0.994$ for $K{=}2$ and $R^2 = 0.974$ for $K{=}4$; the residual variance reflects MC sampling noise rather than model misspecification, since Theorem~\ref{thm:bias_identity} is an exact identity at the population level.
42	In 50\% of configurations (260/520, excluding $\Delta_c{=}0$ rows where bias is zero by construction), global correction produces larger absolute bias than the naive estimator.
43	The damage concentrates in low-$\pi$ subgroups: among subgroups where $\pi_s < \bar{\pi}$, global correction increases bias in 84.6\% of cases.
44	Maximum observed amplification reaches 2.86$\times$ (K=2) and 2.41$\times$ (K=4) relative to the naive estimator.
45	Figure~\ref{fig:heatmap} visualizes the $\Delta\pi \times \Delta\tau$ amplification surface across the parameter grid.
46	
47	\begin{figure*}[t]
48	\centering
49	\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{figures/fig2_heatmap.pdf}
50	\caption{Bias amplification under global correction across the $\Delta\pi \times \Delta\tau$ parameter grid ($K{=}2$). (a) Low-error subgroup: global correction always helps (ratio $< 1$). (b) High-error subgroup: when $\Delta\pi > 0.12$ (dashed line), global correction \emph{increases} bias relative to the naive estimator (hatched region), with amplification reaching 2.86$\times$.}
51	\label{fig:heatmap}
52	\end{figure*}
53	
54	\subsection{EC-HTE Evaluation}
55	\label{sec:ec_hte_eval}
56	
57	Table~\ref{tab:main_results} presents the main results across representative configurations.
58	In the synthetic DGP with $K{=}2$ subgroups and extreme misclassification heterogeneity, HB EC-HTE reduces $|\text{bias}|$ from 0.059 (global) to 0.011 (a 5.4$\times$ reduction) while maintaining nominal coverage (0.95) and comparable RMSE (0.093 vs.\ 0.099).
59	The advantage persists at $K{=}4$: EC-HTE achieves $|\text{bias}|{=}0.009$ versus 0.056 for global (6.2$\times$ reduction), though with a small RMSE penalty (0.127 vs.\ 0.125).
60	Under moderate heterogeneity ($K{=}2$), global correction already achieves low bias (0.009), and EC-HTE provides negligible improvement (0.005) at the cost of slightly higher RMSE (0.075 vs.\ 0.074).
61	This illustrates the conditional nature of EC-HTE's advantage: when $\Delta\pi$ is small, the variance cost of stratification is not offset by bias reduction.
62	
63	In the semi-synthetic TweetEval experiment, the pattern shifts.
64	Global correction achieves the lowest $|\text{bias}|$ (0.023) among non-oracle methods, while HB EC-HTE attains 0.027 with substantially higher RMSE (0.225 vs.\ 0.124).
65	This is consistent with moderate $\Delta\pi{=}0.20$ and the high-error subgroups (S2, S3) comprising only 23\% of data: the bias reduction from stratification is marginal while the variance cost of four per-subgroup confusion matrices is substantial.
66	HB EC-HTE does improve over stratified MLE (RMSE 0.225 vs.\ 0.248), confirming that partial pooling helps, but the improvement is insufficient to overcome the structural variance from unbalanced subgroup sizes.
67	At $n_{\text{expert}} \geq 250$, HB and MLE converge to within 5\% on all metrics.
68	
69	\paragraph{CausalForest K-dependence.}
70	When the downstream estimator is a CausalForest~\cite{wager2018causal} rather than difference-in-means, the bias mechanism operates with amplified magnitude.
71	At $K{=}4$/extreme/$n{=}500$, EC-HTE Forest reduces $|\text{bias}|$ from 0.191 (global) to 0.040, a 4.8$\times$ improvement with lower RMSE (0.224 vs.\ 0.244) and dramatically better coverage (0.91 vs.\ 0.58).
72	The debiasing-hurts phenomenon intensifies: global correction amplifies naive bias by up to 5.9$\times$ in the worst subgroup (compared to 2.41$\times$ for difference-in-means), because the forest's sensitivity to covariate noise magnifies the effect of label errors.
73	At $K{=}2$/$n{=}500$, EC-HTE Forest achieves near-zero bias (0.004--0.013 across subgroups) versus 0.033--0.109 for global, with coverage of 0.91 compared to 0.58 for the global variant.
74	At $K{=}4$, the per-subgroup range widens to 0.002--0.068 while coverage remains above 0.80.
75	However, this comes at a variance cost: at $K{=}4$/$n{=}100$, EC-HTE Forest RMSE reaches 1.43 (3.5$\times$ naive), underscoring the budget guidelines in Section~\ref{sec:budget}.
76	
77	\begin{table*}[t]
78	\centering
79	\caption{Main results across synthetic (difference-in-means and CausalForest) and semi-synthetic configurations. $|\text{Bias}|$ and RMSE are averaged over subgroups, $z$-levels, and 100 MC runs. Bold marks lowest $|\text{bias}|$ per block. $^\dagger$RMSE exceeds Global in this configuration, reflecting the variance cost of stratification.}
80	\label{tab:main_results}
81	\small

\section{Experiments}

\subsection{Experimental Setup and Data Generation}

\subsubsection{Synthetic DGP}

We generate data from a controlled data-generating process (DGP) that separates the effect of subgroup-level misclassification heterogeneity from other confounders.
For each observation $i$, the potential outcome under treatment $t$ is
\begin{equation}
Y_i(t) = \alpha + \tau(Z_i) \cdot t + \beta X_i + \varepsilon_i, \quad \varepsilon_i \sim \mathcal{N}(0,1),
\end{equation}
where $T_i \sim \text{Bernoulli}(0.5)$ simulates a randomized controlled trial, and $Z_i \in \{0, \ldots, K{-}1\}$ is the true effect modifier with $K \in \{2, 4\}$ subgroups.
The conditional average treatment effect (CATE) $\tau(Z{=}z)$ varies across subgroups with controlled heterogeneity $\Delta\tau = \max_z \tau(z) - \min_z \tau(z)$.
Misclassification is injected through subgroup-specific symmetric confusion matrices $C_s$: the observed label $\hat{Z}_i$ is drawn as $\hat{Z}_i \sim \text{Multinomial}(C_{S_i})$, where each subgroup $s$ has error rate $\pi_s$ and $\Delta\pi = \max_s \pi_s - \min_s \pi_s$ controls heterogeneity.
We fix $N{=}5000$ observations and vary $n_{\text{expert}} \in \{50, 100, 250, 500, 1000, 2000\}$ (the number of expert-labeled observations used to estimate confusion matrices).
Each configuration is repeated for 100 Monte Carlo runs.

\subsubsection{Semi-synthetic DGP (TweetEval)}

To test EC-HTE under realistic conditions, we construct a semi-synthetic DGP from the TweetEval sentiment corpus~\cite{barbieri2020tweeteval}, sampling $N{=}5000$ tweets per run from a pool of 57{,}899.
Four subgroups are defined by crossing two binary text features: presence of hashtags (\texttt{has\_hashtag}) and text length relative to the median (\texttt{text\_length\_bin}).
This yields unbalanced subgroup proportions (S0: 39\%, S1: 38\%, S2: 12\%, S3: 11\%).
The effect modifier is $Z{=}1$ if the true sentiment is positive ($P(Z{=}1) \approx 35\%$), and $Z{=}0$ otherwise.
We set subgroup-specific misclassification rates $\pi_{S0}{=}0.05$, $\pi_{S1}{=}0.10$, $\pi_{S2}{=}0.15$, $\pi_{S3}{=}0.25$ in the extreme regime, reflecting empirical evidence that hashtag-heavy text degrades LLM classifier accuracy~\cite{ashwin2025bias}.
The outcome model is
\begin{equation}
Y_i = 1.0 + \tau(Z_i, S_i) \cdot T_i + 0.3 \cdot \text{len}_i + 0.2 \cdot \text{mention}_i + \varepsilon_i,
\end{equation}
where $\tau(Z{=}1, S) \in \{0.5, 0.4, 0.3, 0.2\}$ for S0--S3 and $\tau(Z{=}0) = 0.1$ is the baseline effect.

\paragraph{Baselines and metrics.}
We compare: (1) \textit{Naive} (no correction), (2) \textit{Global} (pooled confusion matrix), (3) \textit{Stratified MLE} (per-subgroup MLE without pooling), (4) \textit{HB EC-HTE} (our hierarchical Bayes estimator), (5) \textit{PPCI}~\cite{sui2026ppci}, and (6) \textit{EC-HTE+PPCI} (our combined method).
For the CausalForest estimator~\cite{wager2018causal}, we also compare naive, global, and EC-HTE variants.
Primary metrics are absolute bias $|\text{bias}|$, root mean squared error (RMSE), and 95\% confidence interval coverage, all averaged across subgroups and 100 MC runs.

\subsection{Bias Mechanism Verification}
\label{sec:bias_mechanism}

The bias decomposition identity (Theorem~\ref{thm:bias_identity}) predicts that global correction introduces bias proportional to $\Delta\pi \times \Delta\tau$ at the subgroup level.
We verify this identity empirically across 520 configurations spanning $K \in \{2,4\}$, two misclassification regimes, and six expert budget levels.
Regressing observed subgroup bias on the predicted $\Delta\pi \times \Delta\tau$ product yields $R^2 = 0.994$ for $K{=}2$ and $R^2 = 0.974$ for $K{=}4$; the residual variance reflects MC sampling noise rather than model misspecification, since Theorem~\ref{thm:bias_identity} is an exact identity at the population level.
In 50\% of configurations (260/520, excluding $\Delta_c{=}0$ rows where bias is zero by construction), global correction produces larger absolute bias than the naive estimator.
The damage concentrates in low-$\pi$ subgroups: among subgroups where $\pi_s < \bar{\pi}$, global correction increases bias in 84.6\% of cases.
Maximum observed amplification reaches 2.86$\times$ (K=2) and 2.41$\times$ (K=4) relative to the naive estimator.
Figure~\ref{fig:heatmap} visualizes the $\Delta\pi \times \Delta\tau$ amplification surface across the parameter grid.

\begin{figure*}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{figures/fig2_heatmap.pdf}
\caption{Bias amplification under global correction across the $\Delta\pi \times \Delta\tau$ parameter grid ($K{=}2$). (a) Low-error subgroup: global correction always helps (ratio $< 1$). (b) High-error subgroup: when $\Delta\pi > 0.12$ (dashed line), global correction \emph{increases} bias relative to the naive estimator (hatched region), with amplification reaching 2.86$\times$.}
\label{fig:heatmap}
\end{figure*}

\subsection{EC-HTE Evaluation}
\label{sec:ec_hte_eval}

Table~\ref{tab:main_results} presents the main results across representative configurations.
In the synthetic DGP with $K{=}2$ subgroups and extreme misclassification heterogeneity, HB EC-HTE reduces $|\text{bias}|$ from 0.059 (global) to 0.011 (a 5.4$\times$ reduction) while maintaining nominal coverage (0.95) and comparable RMSE (0.093 vs.\ 0.099).
The advantage persists at $K{=}4$: EC-HTE achieves $|\text{bias}|{=}0.009$ versus 0.056 for global (6.2$\times$ reduction), though with a small RMSE penalty (0.127 vs.\ 0.125).
Under moderate heterogeneity ($K{=}2$), global correction already achieves low bias (0.009), and EC-HTE provides negligible improvement (0.005) at the cost of slightly higher RMSE (0.075 vs.\ 0.074).
This illustrates the conditional nature of EC-HTE's advantage: when $\Delta\pi$ is small, the variance cost of stratification is not offset by bias reduction.

In the semi-synthetic TweetEval experiment, the pattern shifts.
Global correction achieves the lowest $|\text{bias}|$ (0.023) among non-oracle methods, while HB EC-HTE attains 0.027 with substantially higher RMSE (0.225 vs.\ 0.124).
This is consistent with moderate $\Delta\pi{=}0.20$ and the high-error subgroups (S2, S3) comprising only 23\% of data: the bias reduction from stratification is marginal while the variance cost of four per-subgroup confusion matrices is substantial.
HB EC-HTE does improve over stratified MLE (RMSE 0.225 vs.\ 0.248), confirming that partial pooling helps, but the improvement is insufficient to overcome the structural variance from unbalanced subgroup sizes.
At $n_{\text{expert}} \geq 250$, HB and MLE converge to within 5\% on all metrics.

\paragraph{CausalForest K-dependence.}
When the downstream estimator is a CausalForest~\cite{wager2018causal} rather than difference-in-means, the bias mechanism operates with amplified magnitude.
At $K{=}4$/extreme/$n{=}500$, EC-HTE Forest reduces $|\text{bias}|$ from 0.191 (global) to 0.040, a 4.8$\times$ improvement with lower RMSE (0.224 vs.\ 0.244) and dramatically better coverage (0.91 vs.\ 0.58).
The debiasing-hurts phenomenon intensifies: global correction amplifies naive bias by up to 5.9$\times$ in the worst subgroup (compared to 2.41$\times$ for difference-in-means), because the forest's sensitivity to covariate noise magnifies the effect of label errors.
At $K{=}2$/$n{=}500$, EC-HTE Forest achieves near-zero bias (0.004--0.013 across subgroups) versus 0.033--0.109 for global, with coverage of 0.91 compared to 0.58 for the global variant.
At $K{=}4$, the per-subgroup range widens to 0.002--0.068 while coverage remains above 0.80.
However, this comes at a variance cost: at $K{=}4$/$n{=}100$, EC-HTE Forest RMSE reaches 1.43 (3.5$\times$ naive), underscoring the budget guidelines in Section~\ref{sec:budget}.

\section*{Limitations}

\paragraph{Expert budget threshold.}
EC-HTE requires at least $n_{\text{expert}} / K \geq 25$ per subgroup for the hierarchical Bayesian shrinkage estimates to stabilize.
Below this threshold, per-subgroup confusion matrix estimates are too noisy for reliable inversion, and stratified MLE is preferred.
At $n_{\text{expert}} \geq 1000$, HB and stratified MLE converge to within 0.5\% on all metrics, making the hierarchical model unnecessary at large expert budgets.

\paragraph{RMSE tradeoff at small $n$.}
EC-HTE achieves lower bias than global correction but incurs higher variance when the expert budget is small relative to the number of subgroups.
In the most unfavorable configuration ($K{=}4$, extreme, $n_{\text{expert}} \leq 100$), EC-HTE CausalForest RMSE reaches 3.5$\times$ that of the naive estimator.
Practitioners should weigh whether bias or variance is more consequential for their application before adopting subgroup-stratified correction at small sample sizes.

\paragraph{Plug-in standard errors.}
The variance-adjusted CausalForest propagates outcome uncertainty through the inverse confusion matrix $\hat{C}_s^{-1}$ but does not propagate uncertainty from the confusion matrix estimation itself.
This plug-in approximation is reasonable at $n_{\text{expert}} \geq 100$, where confusion matrix estimation variance is small relative to outcome variance, but may understate total uncertainty below this threshold.
Full Bayesian propagation of confusion matrix posterior uncertainty through the causal forest splitting procedure is computationally prohibitive and left to future work.

\paragraph{Symmetric misclassification assumption.}
All experiments use symmetric error rates ($P(\hat{Z}{=}1 \mid Z{=}0) = P(\hat{Z}{=}0 \mid Z{=}1)$).
Real LLM annotators may exhibit asymmetric confusion patterns, such as higher false positive than false negative rates for certain label categories.
The bias decomposition identity (Theorem~\ref{thm:bias_identity}) generalizes to asymmetric matrices, but empirical validation under asymmetric misclassification is left to future work.

\paragraph{Subgroup structure assumed known.}
EC-HTE requires discrete, pre-defined subgroups as input.
Continuous effect modifiers or latent subgroup discovery settings require fundamentally different approaches.
The hierarchical prior provides partial robustness to noisy subgroup definitions through automatic shrinkage toward the global mean, but intersectional subgroups with many levels may exceed the $n_{\text{expert}} / K \geq 25$ budget threshold, limiting practical applicability to settings with moderate $K$.
